JPMorgan said in a note on Wednesday that the global oil market moved back into surplus after months of disruption tied to conflict in the Middle East. The bank estimates the market swung to a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September and widened to 1.4 million bpd in October, driven by recovering exports from the Middle East, higher output from other regions and weaker global demand.

...

Key Points

* JPMorgan estimates the global oil market was in a surplus of 1.1 million bpd in September and 1.4 million bpd in October, close to last years average surplus of 1.3 million bpd.
* Global crude imports rose to 44.9 million bpd in October, up 1.3 million bpd from a year earlier, and inventories and trade flows indicate excess barrels are returning to the market.
* Middle Eastern exports recovered to around 20.7 million bpd from a low of 9.8 million bpd in March, and Latin America supplied about 1.5 million bpd more crude than a year ago, led by Brazil, Venezuela, Guyana and Argentina - impacts felt across the energy sector, oil trading, and downstream refining.
